# Delegation protocol

Delegate only when isolated context, specialization, useful parallelism, or disposable exploration outweighs coordination. Otherwise root works. Root remains controller, integrator, and completion owner. Each child satisfies one named evidence/signoff need rather than duplicating root work. A child has no controller, integration, landing, external-action, completion, or delegation authority.

Read-only is default. A mutation lease names its isolated worktree or paths, permitted edits and commands, required check, and stop condition. Independent isolated worktrees may hold concurrent bounded mutation leases only when their paths, decisions, dependencies, integration targets, landing surfaces, authority, and external effects do not overlap. A shared worktree has one writer. Root waits for every mutating lease to close before it integrates, lands, changes phase, operates on worktrees, or completes.

Before dispatch record goal, active stage, source or path, expected benefit, mode, ownership, allowed commands, forbidden paths or actions, named evidence/signoff need, required verification, and stop condition. An assessment is read-only evidence, not mutation authority. A child may not change instructions, provider state, configuration outside its lease, commit, push, merge, publish, use credentials, act externally, or delegate.

On crossed scope, competing ownership, or unauthorized action: interrupt, inspect status and diff, preserve unrelated work, and reject unverified output. Root verifies accepted evidence and the final diff.

Pass only needed context and use only completed results. A child stops when that need is met or its assignment ends. Return only conclusion or diff summary, evidence, verification, uncertainty, and blockers.
# Lifecycle protocol

## Durable goals

Root creates or reuses goals only for multi-step, long-running, or restart-prone work. Goals record progress, never authority. Keep simple tasks goal-free. Complete only when no required work remains; block only after safe in-scope alternatives are exhausted.

## Plans

Keep plans concise, ordered, and in scope. Record controller, stage, authoritative artifact, owners, approval boundary, stop condition, and open questions. Plans may select tools and bounded workers, never broaden authority. One writer owns each worktree.

Execute accepted plans. Ask only at explicit gates for material product, scope, authority, risk, irreversible, external-effect, or user-owned choices. Reconcile when evidence requires a material scope or risk change.

## Execution economics

Before durable goal or plan work, root checks fresh capability and metering evidence already in context.

Record available harness and model CLIs; metering class; remaining quota and reset; historical actual cost or tokens; privacy and organization constraints; required capability and reasoning; source class, observation time, and freshness.

Unavailable or stale evidence is unknown. Missing telemetry alone does not block. History is not a future estimate. Root owns model, effort, and provider choice. Management does not collect telemetry or invoke providers.

## Controller ownership

Root remains controller, sole integrator, and completion owner. One lifecycle or stage controller is active at a time. Bounded workers do not inherit control. Reject overlapping lifecycle, planning, writing, delegation, integration, or landing ownership.

## Handoffs

A controller handoff requires a verified checkpoint naming the outgoing controller, completed stage, authoritative artifact and accepted findings, incoming controller, scope changes, outgoing-controller inactivity, and verification owner. Root verifies that checkpoint before activation. Informational handoffs transfer no authority.

## Review findings

Review findings are candidate evidence, not automatic work. Discovery importance and blocker eligibility are independent. Only blocks-now findings backed by evidence already anchored in the verified current revision may interrupt; observed evidence cannot admit its own block. The boundary criterion includes authority, safety, destructive action, and external effect. Decision-required is terminal and claim-scoped, creates no pending proposal, and leaves unrelated work running. Deferred findings do not change the active contract. One focused rereview after admitted repairs is the maximum current-stage loop.

Model or reasoning effort never changes scope, authority, verification obligations, or blocker eligibility.

## Reconciliation

After approved artifact changes, reconcile downstream plans before mutation. At each stage boundary confirm outcome, state, verification, approval boundary, and next action. Goals, plans, and handoffs never authorize publishing, destructive work, credentials, or external action.
# VCS

Inspect status/diff,upstream/divergence,remote/base/head,dup-PR/auth; preserve unrelated; hunk-stage.
Branch {repo rule;team=`<conventional-type>/<forge-username>/<short-kebab-summary>`;solo=`<conventional-type>/<short-kebab-summary>`;trusted repo/forge, not email;no agent/model/harness/vendor prefix;published: authority}.
Commit {discover repo format/limit first;lines <= limit, 100 if absent;subject-only/wrap;hooks enforce/not discover;commit auth != push}.

Concern commits; generated+source. Prepush: fold same-concern correction into owner commit; no trailing fixup. Postpush: additive iff independent|required|no scoped rewrite authority.

Map{lightweight;stale=scope change|CI repair/test/simplify/complete prior|later same-concern|gen/dependency move|post-PR}. Gates{prepush|stable/pre-final-CI|final handoff/readiness}: inspect{range,status/diff,upstream/divergence,later/earlier}; classify{independent,fixup,squash,obsolete}. Provisional CI push != ready; F/S/O blocks only when commit history is review input.
Unpushed rewrite iff {current task;unpublished/unshared;one owner;no prior-user/unrelated;same scope/tree/evidence;unprotected;repo allows}; finish grants no commit/landing. Else ask.
Pushed repair: direct user task/correction request authorizes owner fixup; no second ask. Require {current unprotected single-owner task branch;lease match;no tag/shared/prior-user/unrelated rewrite;requested scope/tree;rerun invalidated checks}; else ask exact branch/map. Reconcile once; force-with-lease; verify remote head. No proposed count-only/squash-merge rewrite.

Confirmed PR URL/base/head/draft first after repo gates; CI/review/long/monitor separate/bounded.
Push=>one current-head batch. Wait terminal unless unsafe/costly/harmful/stuck/user-now: {success/failure/cancel/timeout/dependency-skip}; no indefinite fail-fast wait. Classify product/infra/flaky; dedupe; one local repair pre-edit; invalidated+mandatory checks; history once; verify tree/history; push once. New head=>new batch.
Verify local/upstream/live

# XState in the engine: what decides, what executes (15 Nov)

## In plain words

The rebuild kept state machines for six things, but only four were built, and those four are thin:
they say "is this move allowed?" and nothing else. The parts that broke tonight (landing, catching
up with main, review, reminding agents) never got a machine. Their rules live in `if` statements
spread over seven files, so a fix in one place misses another.

This plan adds three machines, most valuable first:

1. **Landing**: one place that says what happens when main moves, a real clash appears, a check fails
   (because of the work, or because of main), the reviewer answers, or you approve.
2. **Agent attention**: one place that decides when Orca may wake an agent. It wakes only for something
   new it can act on, never for the same state again.
3. **Decisions**: questions waiting for you (open, snoozed, answered, dismissed, expired).

Machines decide; the existing durable procedures still do the work. One small new table (attention).
Each machine lands on its own, tested from its own diagram.

## 1. Inventory: where the engine keeps state

| Area | Where state lives today | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Work lifecycle | `work_item.lifecycle`, `work/lifecycle.machine.ts` | Machine exists (decide only). Keep. |
| Session episode | `session.status`, `sessions/session.machine.ts` | Machine exists. Keep. |
| Copy | `copy.state`, `copies/copy.machine.ts` + `transition.ts` | Machine exists; `transition.ts` is the best commit path today (CAS + retry). Keep as the model. |
| Update | `update_run.state`, `update/coordinator.machine.ts` | Machine exists. Keep. |
| **Landing** | `landing_batch.state` (11 values, mirrored to `landing_entry.state`), `repo.advance(id, state, patch, from?)` with hand-written `from` lists in `Landing.ts` (lines 256, 361, 760, 768, 782), outcome kinds `again/failed/paused/stopped/landed` in `round()` | **Add machine.** Highest value. |
| Landing place | `landing_place.catch_ups`, `last_main`; `order.ts` `landingBlocker` (`catchUps >= 2`) | Stays a scoring function, but the "count a catch-up" rule becomes a guarded action of the landing machine. |
| Catch-up attempt | `landing_catch_up(item, main_sha)` row, `catch-up.ts` | Stays a pipeline (it is an idempotent Git step). Its result becomes an event. |
| **Agent wake / delivery** | `notice.evaluated_under` marker `result|contents|count` in `sessions/delivery.ts`; `wake` flag in `Notices.post` (w/next-batch); `hear()` in `Landing.ts`; `ready.ts:315`; ~20 `inputs.send` call sites | **Add machine** for the item's coordinator (system/notice wakes only). |
| **Requests** | `request.state` (`open/answered/dismissed/expired`) + `snoozed_until`, checks scattered in `Requests.ts` (`row.state !== "open"` x8) | **Add machine.** Lower value; mostly consolidation. |
| Check run | `check_run.state` (launching/running/passed/failed/uncertain/cancelled) | Stays a procedure (`check.run.v1`); linear, reconcile is per step. |
| Review | `review_result`, `ReviewerPool` | Stays a procedure; its verdict is a landing event. |
| Inputs, procedure runs, notices | `input.state`, `procedure_run.state`, `notice.state` | Queue, executor, keyed upsert. Not machines. |
| Governor, retries, cleanup scan, storage, agent turns | — | Rebuild's "not statecharts" list kept. |

## 2. Machines to add

### Kernel (shared, built once in task 1)

`apps/server/src/core/machine/kernel.ts`, ~60 lines, generalising `copies/transition.ts`:

```
decide(machine, state, event, facts) → Option<{ to, patch, intents }>
```

Pure, using only `initialTransition` / `transition` / `isUnhandled`. Intents are emitted actions
(`enq.emit({ type: "intent.…" })`), as the deleted `machines/kernel.ts` did; timers, `invoke` and
spawned actors are rejected as defects. A small `commit(repo, id, event)` runs: read row → decide →
one `Db.tx` (versioned `apply` with CAS on `version`, journal entry, then run intents that are DB
writes inside the same tx; intents that wake an agent or touch Git are recorded as inputs/notices
inside the tx, never executed). On `Conflict`, re-read and decide once (as `transition.ts` does).
Unhandled → typed `Refused` with the machine's plain-words reason. No `machine_state` snapshot
table: state is the existing column; context is the row's facts.

Intent vocabulary (closed union): `patch` (columns), `notice.post` / `notice.resolve` (keyed),
`input.send` (via the attention machine only), `place.countCatchUp`, `place.release`,
`procedure.start`.

### A. Landing (aggregate `landing_batch`, column `landing_batch.state`)

States (existing values, no migration): `queued → merging → checking → reviewing →
awaiting_owner | held → publishing → (awaiting_pr →) landed`; terminals `failed`, `removed`.

| Event (fact from caller) | From | To / guard | Intents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SELECTED` | queued | merging | patch reason=null |
| `WAITING{reason}` | queued | queued, only if reason changed | patch reason |
| `NOTHING_READY` | queued | failed | notice |
| `GATHERED{base,tree,fingerprint}` | merging | checking | patch base/tree/fingerprint |
| `MAIN_MOVED_CLEAN{main}` | merging, checking, reviewing, awaiting_owner, publishing | merging; guard `round < 3` else failed("main kept changing") | **no** catch-up count, **no** agent wake, keep review verdict (diff-keyed, from w/next-batch) |
| `CLASH{main, files}` | merging, publishing | failed | `place.countCatchUp(main)` once per main (guard `last_main != main`), notice `landing-stuck` if `catch_ups >= 2`, attention `CLASH` |
| `CATCH_UP_BLOCKED{reason}` | merging | failed | attention `LANDING_FAILED`; no count (w/next-batch rule) |
| `CHECK_FAILED{cause}` | checking | `cause=item` → failed (or split if >1 entry); `cause=main` → held + project notice "main's own check is failing"; `cause=unknown` → failed | item: attention `CHECK_FAILED`; main: **no** agent wake |
| `CHECKS_PASSED` | checking | reviewing | resolve check faults |
| `REVIEW{verdict}` | reviewing | ready → decide; fixes → failed; escalate → awaiting_owner; unavailable → failed (review-stopped notice, no wake) | attention `REVIEW_FINDINGS` for fixes |
| `DECIDED{level}` | reviewing | orca → publishing; owner → awaiting_owner; hold → held | — |
| `OWNER_APPROVED` | awaiting_owner, held | publishing; guard `approved_at` unset | patch approved_at |
| `OWNER_PARKED` | awaiting_owner | held | — |
| `PUBLISHED{commit}` / `PR_OPENED` / `PR_MERGED` | publishing / awaiting_pr | landed / awaiting_pr / publishing | release places, resolve notices, tell |
| `REMOVED{reason}` | any non-terminal | removed | notice; attention none |
| `INTERNAL_FAULT` | any non-terminal | failed | notice; no wake |

`cause` comes from recorded facts: `main` when the command passed on the item's caught-up copy
(ready-to-land run) and also fails on main's own tree at `base_sha`; `item` when it passes there;
else `unknown`. The main-tree run happens only on failure, once per (`base_sha`, command).

Plug-in: `Landing.ts` keeps `landing.v1` and its steps; each `advance(batchId, X, …)` becomes
`landingMachine.send(batchId, EVENT)`. `round()`'s `Outcome` kinds map 1:1 to events, and the
`fail` closing step's per-entry `why` strings become the machine's notice intents. `ready.ts`,
`catch-up.ts` and `stuck.ts` stop calling `countCatchUp`/`notifyStuck` directly; they return facts.

### B. Agent attention (aggregate: work item coordinator; new table `agent_attention`)

The one rule tonight kept breaking: *wake an agent only for a new actionable fact*.

Context: `{ result_key, contents_key, reminders, last_wake_ref }`.
States: `quiet` (nothing owed), `owed` (a wake is queued as an input), `waiting` (agent turn running;
deliver held inputs at turn end), `stalled` (reminder cap reached; owner notice, no more wakes),
`off` (item not active, owner asks > 0, or session gone).

| Event | Guard | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `LANDING_FAILED{entry,state}` / `CLASH` / `CHECK_FAILED` / `REVIEW_FINDINGS` | `result_key` differs | → owed; `input.send` with sourceRef `attention:<item>:<result_key>`; reminders=0 |
| same event, same `result_key` | — | ignored (unhandled → no-op, not refused) |
| `CHECK_PASSED{othersRunning}` | `othersRunning` | hold input, no wake (w/next-batch rule) |
| `AGENT_STOPPED{contents, queued}` | `queued` (ready pending/landing open) | stay |
| | contents changed **and** reminders < cap | → owed; reminder; reminders+1 |
| | contents unchanged, or reminders ≥ cap | → stalled; post `delivery-stopped` notice; **no input** |
| `TURN_STARTED` / `TURN_ENDED` | — | owed→waiting→quiet |
| `ITEM_PAUSED` / `OWNER_ASK_OPENED` | — | → off; resolve delivery notice |
| `ITEM_RESUMED` / `OWNER_ASK_SETTLED` | — | → quiet |

The per-result cap (today a literal `3` in `delivery.ts`, labelled shortcut) becomes a guard
parameter read from `limits.ts`, still labelled stopgap until stall detection exists (memory
`monitor-not-hardcode`). Owner and agent-to-agent messages bypass this machine: they always wake.

Persistence: one additive migration `agent_attention(work_item_id PK, state, result_key,
contents_key, reminders, version, updated_at)`. Why: today the marker lives in
`notice.evaluated_under`, and retention purges resolved notices, silently re-arming reminders.
Backfill from the `delivery` notice marker.

Call sites routed through it: `Landing.ts hear()`, `ready.ts:315`, `sessions/delivery.ts`,
`checks/Checks.ts:382` (via `Notices.post deliverTo`), `agent-tools/own-checks.ts`,
`Sessions.ts:177` (no-tool-call nudge). Other `inputs.send` sites (owner, resume, crash retry,
reviewer, rebalance) stay as they are.

### C. Request/decision (aggregate `request`, column `request.state` + `snoozed_until`)

States: `open.awake`, `open.snoozed` (derived from `snoozed_until`, so no new value), `answered`,
`dismissed`, `expired`. Events: `ANSWER{by}`, `DISMISS{by}`, `REPLACED`, `WORK_ENDED`, `SNOOZE{until}`
(guard class = `owner_decision`), `UNSNOOZE`, `SNOOZE_DUE`, `EXPIRE`. Intents: patch, journal,
`input.send` of the answer to the asking session (today `Requests.ts:205`), resolve owner notice.
Idempotency: `ANSWER` with the same `by` and words from `answered` is handled (returns row), matching
`Requests.ts:351`.

## 3. `@xstate/effect`

It runs actors in memory: `createEffectActor`, `invoke` of Effect logic, `after` timers. That is
exactly what the kernel forbids, because work would run outside the commit and vanish on restart.
`landing.v1` and other procedures already give durability (steps, idempotency keys, reconcile).

**Recommendation:** do not use its actors. Use two pure helpers only:
- `toStandardSetupSchemas` / `toStandardSchema`: declare machine event and context schemas with the
  Effect `Schema` already in contracts, so events from RPC/procedures are decoded once.
- `taggedState` + `Match.exhaustive` for exhaustive handling of states in views (`work-state.ts`).

If they break on an alpha bump, drop them and remove the dependency.

## 4. Testing

1. **Graph tests per machine.** `xstate/graph` ships in `6.0.0-alpha.69` (`getShortestPaths`,
   `getSimplePaths`, `getAdjacencyMap`); confirm after the alpha.73 bump, else a 30-line BFS over
   `transition()`. For every reachable state and event: decide is total (handled or refused with
   words), terminals accept nothing, and each shortest path to `landed` replays against a real
   `LandingRepo` on a temporary DB with the same end row.
2. **Invariants (property tests over random event sequences):**
   - Landing: a sequence of only `MAIN_MOVED_CLEAN` never reaches `failed` before round 3, never
     increments `catch_ups`, never emits `input.send`, and keeps the review verdict.
   - Landing: `catch_ups` increases at most once per distinct `main`, only on `CLASH`.
   - Landing: `CHECK_FAILED{cause:"main"}` never wakes the item's agent.
   - Attention: no `input.send` without an event whose `result_key` or `contents_key` is new; at
     most `cap` reminders per `result_key`; `off` emits nothing.
   - Requests: only `owner_decision` can be snoozed; a settled request accepts nothing but its own
     idempotent repeat.
3. **Misbehaving-agent tests** (`apps/server/src/core/testing/chaos*`): add/turn green:
   S10 (clash ignored), S12 (landing fails, agent idle) asserting wake counts; a new S18 "main moves
   cleanly five times during review" (no wake, lands); S19 "main's own check is red" (item held,
   agent not woken). Each new guarantee starts as `it.fails`, flips with its task.

## 5. Migration

- Landing and requests: zero schema change; machine states are the existing column values.
  `awaiting_pr` keeps its CHECK list.
- Attention: one additive migration (next number from `migrate.ts`), forward-only, backfilled.
- Cutover per machine with no flag: one task replaces every writer of that column in one change, and
  a grep test (`arch.test.ts` style) forbids direct writes to the column outside the machine's
  `send` (e.g. no `repo.advance(` calls outside `landing/machine.ts`).
- Order: kernel + landing, then attention, then requests. Each lands alone.

## 6. Briefs for Codex (gpt-6.1-sol)

All tasks: start from `main` **after w/next-batch and w/deps-upgrade land**. Read `AGENTS.md`. Rules: never change `HOME`; never touch `~/.orca*`; no push, no
PR; commits signed (`git commit -S`); do not widen confinement or sandbox settings; lint only changed
files (`pnpm exec vp lint <files>`); run suites in the foreground; minimal comments; no new
dependencies. Verify each with: `pnpm -r --workspace-concurrency=1 run typecheck`, the affected
server tests, then `pnpm --filter @orca/server test`, `pnpm --filter @orca/contracts test`,
`node scripts/hygiene.ts`, and `orca_run_check`/direct runs of `.orca/landing.json` checks touched.
Include db/arch/column-cap/migration rule tests (`arch.test.ts`, `db` tests).

## Addendum (15 Nov): `@xstate/effect` revisited

The owner asked to use more of `@xstate/effect`. Its v6 docs (quick-start and actors pages) remove the main objection above: actors can be persisted with `actor.getPersistedSnapshot()` and restored with `createEffectActor(logic, { snapshot })` in another process without re-running entry actions; pending `after` timers keep their original deadline on Effect's `Clock` (overdue ones fire on start); running Effect tasks and streams restart, so they must be idempotent. `createSnapshotCodec(machine, schema)` gives schema-checked JSON snapshots and `machineVersions(...).migrateSnapshot` gives versioned migrations. Logic uses Effect services (`Context.Service`, `Effect.provideService`) and `TestClock`, and leaving a state interrupts its invoked Effect.

Revised use, in order:
1. Timers as machine transitions (`after`) on Effect `Clock`, tested with `TestClock`: delivery reminder delays, decision snooze (`snoozed_until`), stall detection for proof-of-life, retry backoff. Replaces load-dependent timeout tests with deterministic ones.
2. Every persisted machine stores a versioned snapshot through `createSnapshotCodec` + `machineVersions` migrations instead of hand-made marker strings (the delivery `evaluated_under` marker is the cautionary case).
3. In-process lifecycles become scoped Effect actors (`setupEffect`, `createEffectLogic`, `createEffectActor`, `send`, `waitFor`): agent turn (start/stream/interrupt), check run, preview and terminal processes, sign-off runner, dev launcher drain/takeover/handback.
4. Landing, attention and decisions keep the pure, DB-atomic kernel, because a state change and its domain writes must commit in one transaction with CAS on `version`. Spike: whether an Effect actor's action can perform the kernel's `Db.tx` so persistence stays atomic; adopt actors there only if it can.

Follow-up Codex tasks (after Task 1): (5) snapshot codec + versioning for existing machines; (6) timers via `after` + `TestClock` for reminders and snooze; (7) agent-turn and check-run lifecycle actors; (8) the atomicity spike.

=== codebase-quality-audit
# Codebase quality audit (15 Nov)

Read-only audit of commit `fa515bf5a`. Effect is covered by a separate audit, and new XState machines by `2026-11-15-xstate-engine.md`. Evidence is grep counts and file:line references. I did not run any lint, fallow, test or build command (the audit copy has no `node_modules`), so tool-only checks are marked "verify".

## In plain words

Overall the code is in better shape than you would expect from code nobody reviewed. The rules in AGENTS.md are mostly followed and many are enforced by machines: database access goes through one door, comments are sparse and explain why, real-process tests outnumber mocked ones, shadcn controls are used almost everywhere, and the old homegrown web store is gone. The weak spots are where things were built twice or kept as temporary stand-ins during the engine rebuild.

Top 5 risks:

1. **Settings screens can spin forever.** Seven "load when the screen opens" hooks discard their errors. If a read fails, the screen shows a loading skeleton with no reason and no retry.
2. **Two test files never run before landing.** The landing test groups pick files by path prefix, and two folders fall between the groups, including the main sandbox test.
3. **The network sandbox is built twice.** Two separate modules set up the agent proxy, and 15 imports reach into the sandbox library's private files. A library upgrade or a fix to only one copy could quietly weaken confinement.
4. **Raw error text reaches the owner.** About 100 screen spots show `error.message` as it arrives. Some of those messages carry process IDs, schema decoder output or "Not connected".
5. **Web data is cached twice.** TanStack Query is called with no caching, and the results are copied into 25 hand-made atoms. There is no `useMutation` anywhere, so 60 components track their own "problem" text and 48 track their own "busy" flag.

## Findings by area

Severity: **High** = bug or a hazard to a security or landing guarantee. **Medium** = maintainability hazard or rule violation. **Low** = style or cleanup.

### 1. Web app (React 19, TanStack, shadcn)

- **High: failed loads look like loading forever.** `apps/web/src/lib/sync.ts:490-701` has 7 hooks shaped like `useEffect(() => { if (open) void core.loadX(); }, [open])` (skill packs, connections, previews, designs, house rules, storage, lessons). Each screen then treats `null` as "still loading", for example `skills-settings.tsx:188`, `storage-settings.tsx:153` and `house-rules-settings.tsx:288` (`if (x === null) return <LoadingSkeleton/>`). A rejected load is an unhandled promise, and the screen never says why. This goes against the owner's "failure states say why" rule.
- **Medium: a homegrown cache sits on top of TanStack Query.** `lib/core/client.ts:254` calls `query.query({ …, staleTime: 0, gcTime: 0 })`, so Query only removes duplicate in-flight requests. The results are copied into 25 `createAtom` stores (`client.ts:173-204`). About 40 action wrappers in `sync.ts` follow the same "command, then reload" pattern (for example `installSkillPack` and `addHouseRule`) where `invalidateQueries` would do. The repo has 58 `useQuery` uses and 0 `useMutation`. 60 components hold `useState<string | null>` problem text and 48 hold busy/saving flags, which is the state
- **Medium: more round trips than needed.** `client.ts:308-319` (`loadPreviews` and `loadDesigns`) makes one list call and then one call per row.
- **Medium: placeholder screens left over from the rebuild.** `lib/core/placeholders.ts` stubs 5 areas: learning, usage history, queued inputs, evidence and settings. There are 77 references to `nothing` / `NotInNewEngineError`. The stub text "This isn't available in the rebuilt engine yet" is owner-facing and mentions engine internals.
- **Medium (verify): React Compiler lint may not run.** The `react-compiler/*` rules live in `apps/web/vite.config.ts:150-160`. The root `vite.config.ts:11` says Vite+ reads lint config only from the root, the root config has no react-hooks plugin, and `apps/web/package.json` has no lint script. If that is true, the compiler's own diagnostics are never enforced. To check, run `vp lint` on a file that breaks `react-compiler/set-state-in-effect`.
- **Low: hand-written memoization still present.** `transcript.tsx:448` (`useCallback`), `transcript.tsx:834` (`useMemo`), `workspace/dismiss.ts:21` and `lib/draft.ts:190` break the "React Compiler, no manual memo" rule.
- **Low: data loading in one-off effects.** There are 80 `useEffect` (12 in `sync.ts`) against 1 `use()`. Heavy panels load lazily (8 `lazy()`), and routes are bundled on purpose (`apps/web/vite.config.ts:118`).
- **Good:** the legacy `lib/store.ts` is gone. Only 3 raw controls exist outside `components/ui`, and all are legitimate. No `onClick` sits on a `div` or `span`. The 58 `oxlint-disable` comments each give a reason. Largest files: `composer.tsx` 1373 lines, `client.ts` 1136.

### 2. Server (non-Effect)

- **High: the sandbox network proxy exists twice.** `core/sandbox/agent.ts:14-19,79-81` (419 lines) and `harness/sandbox.ts:19-22,421-422` (616 lines) each build HTTP and SOCKS proxies. `core/sandbox/agent.ts:24` also imports helpers back from `harness/sandbox.ts`. 15 imports in 8 files reach into `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime/dist/sandbox/*.js`, which is the package's private build output. That package is at 0.0.81, so any release can move those files.
- **Medium: architecture rules cover only half the server.** `core/arch.test.ts:10` scans only `src/core`. The top-level `src/harness` (54 files), `src/routing`, `src/usage` and `src/learning` are not checked. The "harness never reaches terminals" rule (`arch.test.ts:74`) therefore checks only the 5-file `core/harness` shim, while the real harness lives in `src/harness`. Direct `node:sqlite` use outside `core/db` exists in `harness/opencode-key.ts:5`, `harness/opencode-v2-driver.ts:7` and `usage/query.ts:7`. These read other tools' databases, which may be legitimate, but no rule covers them. C
- **Medium: the Codex protocol ignores what it doesn't understand.** `harness/codex-protocol.ts:1-2` keeps a hand-maintained subset of `codex app-server` types (from codex-cli 0.163 to 0.166) and states that "a line or field that does not match is ignored". After a Codex update, events could disappear without an error. Nothing compares these types with the installed `generate-ts` output.
- **Medium: very large modules.** `harness/codex.ts` 1514 lines, `harness/acp.ts` 1182, `testing/previews.ts` 1181, `core/skills/skill-packs.ts` 1178, `harness/pi.ts` 1131, `harness/claude.ts` 1062, `core/checks/execution-groups.ts` 922.
- **Medium: production code imports test budgets.** `core/engine-control/Diagnostics.ts:19` imports `../testing/budgets.ts`.
- **Medium: raw error text reaches the owner.** 16 places pass `String(error)` or `error.message` as a `reason`, for example `core/settings/Settings.ts:58` (schema decoder text), `core/launcher/launcher.ts:65` (a pid), `core/update/builder.ts:154` and `harness/acp.ts:1004` (agent stderr). On the web side, `lib/errors.ts` `errorMessage` passes this text through to about 100 UI spots. `plainError` only strips a leading "Error:".
- **Good:** no `TODO`/`FIXME`/`HACK` markers. The `shortcut:` comments use the house format. Comments make up about 4% of server lines and explain why rather than restate code. The 10 fallow ignores are all for crash children started by path.

### 3. XState (the 4 machines)

`copies/copy.machine.ts` (140 lines), `sessions/session.machine.ts` (67), `work/lifecycle.machine.ts` (63) and `update/coordinator.machine.ts` (53) all follow the same idiomatic pattern: a pure decision from `createMachine` + `resolveState` + `transition` + `isUnhandled`, with no actors and no side effects. That pattern suits an engine that persists state in SQLite.

/// <reference types="node" />
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { git, repoRoot } from "./test-baselines.ts";

const TYPES = ["feat", "fix", "refactor", "perf", "test", "docs", "style", "build", "ci", "chore", "revert"];
const TYPED = new RegExp(`^(?:${TYPES.join("|")})(?:\\([a-z0-9-]+\\))?!?: \\S`, "u");

// Git writes these titles itself.
const GENERATED = /^(?:Merge |Revert "|fixup! |squash! |amend! )/u;

const titleOf = (message: string) => message.split("\n").find(line => line.trim() !== "" && !line.startsWith("#")) ?? "";

export const typed = (message: string) => GENERATED.test(titleOf(message)) || TYPED.test(titleOf(message));

/** Titles of the commits after `base` that lack a conventional type. */
export const untyped = (root: string, base = "main") => git(root, "log", "--format=%s", `${base}..HEAD`).split("\n").filter(title => title !== "" && !typed(title));

export const advice = (titles: readonly string[]) => `Start each commit title with a type, like "fix: Keep the reason plain" (${TYPES.join(", ")}):\n${titles.map(title => `  ${title}`).join("\n")}`;

if (import.meta.main) {
  const [file] = process.argv.slice(2);
  const bad = file === undefined ? untyped(repoRoot) : [readFileSync(file, "utf-8")].flatMap(message => typed(message) ? [] : [titleOf(message)]);

  if (bad.length > 0) {
    console.error(advice(bad));
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local signoff: run CIVIC's checks on this machine instead of paid CI minutes, then
# record a green "signoff" commit status on GitHub for the exact commit that passed.
#
#   bin/signoff           run public engine and synthetic example checks; post statuses
#   bin/signoff --browser include browser evidence for the public demo
#   bin/signoff --no-post run without posting a status
set -euo pipefail

# The whole gate runs in one temporary folder that is removed afterwards (bin/with-temp-root.mjs).
if [ -z "${CIVIC_TEMP_ROOT:-}" ]; then
  exec node "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/with-temp-root.mjs" bash "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" "$@"
fi

browser=0 post=1
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --browser) browser=1 ;;
    --no-post) post=0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
packages_dir="$repo_root/packages"
graph_dir="$repo_root/graph"
importers_dir="$repo_root/importers"
demo_dir="$repo_root/demo/fluent-button"
card_dir="$repo_root/demo/card"
review_dir="$repo_root/review"
crawl_dir="$repo_root/crawl"
discovery_dir="$repo_root/projects/discovery-app"
step() { printf '\n[signoff %s] %s\n' "$(date +%H:%M:%S)" "$1"; }

# A signoff vouches for one commit, so uncommitted changes would make it a false claim.
if [ -n "$(git -C "$repo_root" status --porcelain)" ]; then
  echo "Commit or stash your changes first: a signoff covers exactly the committed HEAD." >&2
  exit 1
fi
sha="$(git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse HEAD)"

step "CIVIC graph: types, tests and example graphs"
pnpm --dir "$graph_dir" install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir "$graph_dir" run check
pnpm --dir "$graph_dir" test
pnpm --dir "$graph_dir" run validate

step "CIVIC review to agent loop: store, CLI and re-capture"
pnpm --dir "$review_dir" install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir "$review_dir" run check
pnpm --dir "$review_dir" test

step "CIVIC crawl loop: types and tests (one test drives a browser)"
pnpm --dir "$crawl_dir" install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir "$crawl_dir" run check
pnpm --dir "$crawl_dir" test

step "CIVIC importers, the Fluent Button and Card demo graphs, and the discovery example graph"
pnpm --dir "$importers_dir" install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir "$importers_dir" run check
pnpm --dir "$importers_dir" test
node "$demo_dir/build.ts" --check
node "$card_dir/build.ts" --check
node "$repo_root/demo/rebrand/build.ts" --check
node "$discovery_dir/build.ts" --check

# Roadmap step 10: findings are raised at the change that caused it. The gate also compares
# the graphs with where this branch left its base (CIVIC_BASE, origin/main by default) and
# names who each new finding asks and tells; the same summary goes on the pull request below.
base_ref="${CIVIC_BASE:-origin/main}"
since=()
git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base_ref^{commit}" >/dev/null && since=(--since "$base_ref")
step "The gate: civic check on the graphs in civic.check.json against civic.baseline.json${since:+ and $base_ref}"
"$repo_root/bin/civic" check --config "$repo_root/civic.check.json" ${since[@]+"${since[@]}"}
if [ "${#since[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  # Library releases on this branch (step 10): variants left unmapped and overrides broken.
  # Reported, not gating: the gate's conflicts are where someone decides a breaking release.
  step "Library releases since $base_ref"
  release_status=0
  "$repo_root/bin/civic" release --config "$repo_root/civic.check.json" "${since[@]}" || release_status=$?
  if [ "$release_status" = 1 ]; then
    echo "A release above breaks a product override or unmaps a variant; its owners are asked to decide it."
  elif [ "$release_status" != 0 ]; then
    exit "$release_status"
  fi
fi
if [ "$browser" = 1 ]; then
  step "Fluent Button web evidence (Playwright)"
  pnpm --dir "$demo_dir/web" install --frozen-lockfile
  pnpm --dir "$demo_dir/web" run evidence
fi

step "CIVIC packages: canvas, shell and Vite connector, with the canvas examples"
pnpm --dir "$packages_dir" install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir "$packages_dir" run check
pnpm --dir "$packages_dir" test

step "CIVIC packages installed from this commit into an empty app, opened in the standalone canvas"
node "$packages_dir/install.check.mjs"

# Checks may not touch tracked files; if they did, the result no longer describes HEAD.
if [ -n "$(git -C "$repo_root" status --porcelain)" ] || [ "$(git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse HEAD)" != "$sha" ]; then
  echo "The working tree changed while checks ran; not signing off." >&2
  exit 1
fi

scope="graph, review loop, importers, Button, Card and rebrand demos, discovery graph, civic gate, CIVIC packages and their install check"
[ "$browser" = 1 ] && scope="$scope + Button web evidence"
if [ "$post" = 0 ]; then step "Passed for $sha ($scope); status not posted"; exit 0; fi
if ! command -v gh >/dev/null; then step "Passed for $sha ($scope). Install the GitHub CLI (gh) to post the signoff status."; exit 0; fi

pr="$(gh pr view --json number,state --jq 'select(.state == "OPEN") | .number' 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -n "$pr" ] && [ "${#since[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then

# 0010: Projects depend on CIVIC; CIVIC stays independent of connected projects

Status: accepted. Original decision: 2026-10-13; boundary clarified 2026-10-20.

## Decision

CIVIC owns the generic canvas, review shell, Vite connector, manifest contract,
recording and evidence system. A reviewed project owns its adapter, scenario
registry, synthetic seed, runtime entry, and optional canvas extension.

A project installs CIVIC's packages at an explicit version. CIVIC neither vendors
private application source nor requires a named application's checkout,
dependencies, assets, or backend to start or pass its public checks.

Optional local integrations are loaded explicitly from ignored configuration.
Their source, captured images, design references, and validation reports stay
outside tracked CIVIC content. Connecting a project does not authorize changing
its source or accessing production data. Synthetic previews use disposable
runtime state and preserve recorded content identities.

## Verification

Public checks use the synthetic Notebook, Tasks, Team board, Reading list, and
Pantry applications, public component demos, and small purpose-built graph and
importer fixtures. Real-project validation is optional and local.

# Rebuilding CIVIC on Orca's foundations (15 Nov 2026)

## In plain words

The owner asked for four things: CIVIC built the way Orca is (Effect, XState, Electron), CIVIC as an MCP server that agent tools plug into, two new features (find the code behind a selected element, and see which server paths no journey reaches), and a cleanup using what Orca learned.

CIVIC is not rewritten from scratch. Most of it is pure data code (the graph, importers, records) that works and is tested; it stays plain functions. What changes is the part that starts, watches and stops things: previews, the review server, the app server, the desktop window, the MCP server and the request lifecycle. Those move onto Effect (resources that always clean up) and XState (one place that says which move is allowed next).

The order is: first the checks that stop old mistakes coming back, then one install for all of CIVIC, then the shared state-machine kernel and the request machine, then the MCP server, then CIVIC as a project in its own picker, then the two features, then the preview, app-server and desktop lifecycles. Each step lands on its own after its checks pass.

Two things need the owner (listed at the end): whether the stale Orca preview builds in the live store may be deleted, and whether CIVIC may have one install at the repository root.

## 1. Audit: where CIVIC is today

Grounded at `f749b770` (this branch). Counts are from `grep` over tracked source, not lint output.

| Area | Today | Target | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Graph, importers, records (`graph/`, `importers/`, `review/src/store.ts`…) | Plain TypeScript, pure functions, `node --test` | Same | **Keep.** No Effect or XState here; a lint rule keeps it that way. `graph/src/validate.ts` (1057 lines) is a later candidate for Effect `Schema` only if it deletes code. |
| Installs | Five separate pnpm installs (`packages/`, `graph/`, `review/`, `importers/`, `crawl/`), each with its own lockfile | One workspace, one lockfile, one `vp run` | **Change** (S3). Two copies of Effect across lockfiles would break type identity, so this comes before Effect leaves `packages/`. |
| Tooling | `tsc` + `vitest` 5 + `node --test`; no linter, no formatter, no hooks | Vite+: `vp lint` (oxlint), `vp fmt`, `vp test`, `vp run` tasks, `vp staged`, `vp hooks` | **Change** (S1). |
| Test lists | Hardcoded in `package.json` scripts (`node --test a.check.mjs b.check.mjs …`) and `packages/local` `check` (12 `node --check` calls); `bin/signoff` names each directory | Derived by glob / from the workspace | **Change** (S1). |
| Review corrections | Written in AGENTS.md, enforced by hand | Lint rules and tests with a baseline that may only shrink | **Change** (S2). 77 `useEffect` in `packages/canvas/src` + `packages/shell/src`; raw timers in 27 files; 0 `vi.mock` (lock it at 0). |
| Request lifecycle (`review/src/loop.ts`, 628 lines) | `open → claimed → fix-ready → resolved/reopened` as `if` checks; records already carry `@version` | XState machine through a pure kernel; the record's version is the compare-and-set | **Change** (S4). Exact match for Orca's durable kernel. |
| Preview launcher (`review/src/preview/launcher.ts`, `state.ts`) | Hand-written start/attach/stop with a registry and pid+start-time checks | Effect scoped processes + XState lifecycle, `after` timers on Effect `Clock` | **Change** (S9). Behaviour (decision 0021) unchanged. |
| Run service (`packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.mjs`) | One worker per run, 8-worker cap, per-run queue, 30 s call timeout, 30 min idle, version-1 journals | Same rules, Effect-owned workers and timers, run machine | **Change** inside the app server (S10). Journal rules stay exactly as the 18 Oct plan lists them. |
| App server | Not built. The launcher owns the Vite server's lifetime. Plan of 18 Oct (`2026-10-18-0515-feat-effect-app-server-lifecycle-plan.md`) is implementation-ready | Effect host with client presence, Electron main as a client | **Build** (S10) from that plan, with pins updated below. |
| Electron (`packages/local/desktop*.mjs`, 148-line main) | Works; needs `CIVIC_ELECTRON_BINARY`; no `electron` dependency; no branch in title; shares one profile | `electron` as a dev dependency, main process as an Effect program, its own profile per worktree | **Change** (S10). |
| MCP server (`review/src/mcp.ts`, 199 lines) | Hand-written stdio JSON-RPC; tool list and JSON schemas typed by hand | Same tools, input schemas derived from Effect `Schema`, new tools for element location and backend coverage | **Change** (S5). Decision 0006 and D35's narrow write path unchanged. |
| Harness integration (`integrations/claude-code`, `.claude-plugin`, `codex.mcp.json`) | Claude Code plugin (skills, hooks, MCP launcher) and a Codex MCP snippet | One MCP server any harness can use; thin per-harness wrappers that only point at it | **Extend** (S11). No per-harness tool lists: the server lists its tools. |
| CIVIC in its own picker | CIVIC reviews itself as the "Isolated CIVIC" workspace via `civic preview`; no `civic.project.json` for CIVIC's screens | A tracked manifest and scenario registry for CIVIC's own screens | **Build** (S6). CIVIC is public, so this is allowed under decision 0010. |
| Live store growth | `.civic-canvas/projects` holds 79 `orca-worktree-*` folders (1.4 GB) | Bounded retention | **Fix the source** (S9b). See §4. |

## 2. Foundations and pins

Match Orca's current `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (read 15 Nov), not the 18 Oct pins:

- `effect` `~4.0.5` and `@effect/platform-node` `~4.0.5`, with `@effect/platform-node-shared` overridden to `4.0.5` (Orca's reason: 4.1 needs Effect 4.1). Tilde, not caret, for that reason only.
- `xstate` `6.0.0-alpha.73`, `@xstate/effect` `1.0.0-alpha.12` (exact: prereleases), listed in `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`.
- `vite-plus` `^1.6.0`, with `vite` aliased to `npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@1.6.0` so every plugin sees one Vite.
- `electron` `^45.3.2` (dev dependency of `packages/local`), `allowBuilds: electron: true`.
- Caret ranges elsewhere; `pnpx taze major -r -l` and `pnpm audit` before each dependency slice; installs only in worktrees.

Where each tool is used:

- **Effect** owns anything with a lifetime: processes, listeners, workers, file watchers, timers, the MCP server, the app server, Electron main. `Context.Service` and layers only where a service earns a boundary (a test swaps it, or two callers share it).
- **XState** decides; it does not execute. Durable lifecycles (requests) use a pure kernel ported from Orca's `core/machine/kernel.ts`: `initial`, `decide` (rejects any effect other than an emitted intent) and `commit` (read, persist with compare-and-set, retry once on conflict). In-process lifecycles (preview, app server, run, desktop window) use `@xstate/effect` actors with `after` timers on Effect `Clock`, tested with `TestClock`.
- **Graph tests** for every machine: `xstate/graph` `getShortestPaths` over a list of events that covers every event the machine declares (the test fails if one is missing), replay each path through the kernel, check terminals accept nothing.
- The kernel lives in a new small package `packages/core` (`@civic/core`): kernel, graph-test helper, and shared Effect services (process, clock-backed scheduling). This replaces the 18 Oct plan's "no core package" (its KTD1), because the request machine (`review/`) and the app server (`packages/canvas`) both need it.

A decision record, `docs/decisions/0022-effect-xstate-electron-foundations.md`, states these boundaries.

## 3. Corrections become checks

Each rule is a lint rule or a test. Where code already breaks a rule, a committed baseline lists today's count per file; the check fails if a count grows, and the baseline is rewritten only downward.

| Rule | How | Baseline today |
|---|---|---|
| No `useEffect` in CIVIC's UI; named hooks for real external sync | oxlint `no-restricted-syntax`/import rule, per-file baseline | 77 |
| No raw `setTimeout`/`setInterval` outside browser UI glue; Effect `Schedule`/`Clock` | oxlint `no-restricted-globals` in server/CLI code | 27 files (verify) |
| No `vi.mock`, no module mocking | oxlint rule | 0, locked |
| Layering: `graph/` and `importers/` import no `effect`, `xstate`, `node:child_process`; browser code imports no `server/`; nothing imports a connected project | architecture test over all tracked source, globbed | measured in S2 |
| Every check runs under `bin/with-temp-root.mjs` | existing `review/test/temp-root.test.ts`, extended to the derived task list | 0 |
| Commit titles typed (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`…) | `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` + `scripts/commit-type.ts`; `bin/signoff` refuses untyped commits after main | — |
| Pre-commit lints staged files, check only | `vp staged --no-stash`; hooks chain each clone's own `.git/hooks` so Entire keeps working | — |
| Effect language service diagnostics | `@effect/language-service` in `tsconfig` plugins, run in `check` | 0 |
| Short "why"-only comments | review rule in AGENTS.md; anti-slop preset where it applies | — |
| No hardcoded lists of files, scripts or tools | test lists by glob; MCP tool list from one table with `Schema` inputs; signoff steps from the workspace | — |

Tests are end to end and unmocked: real processes, temporary stores, temporary git repositories, Playwright for UI.

## 4. The store leak

The 79 `orca-worktree-*` folders come from the owner's private Orca adapter (`.civic-canvas/private-integrations/runtime/packages/local/orca-worktrees.mjs`, `buildWorktree`). It names a folder per worktree path and adds a new `builds/<hash>-<uuid>` on each change. Nothing removes a folder when its worktree is gone, or old builds once a newer one is published.

That adapter is ignored local storage in the owner's live copy, so it is not edited here. The fix goes in tracked code: a shared retention helper in `packages/local` (keep the newest published build per live worktree and the build a running preview uses; remove builds of worktrees that no longer exist, only inside the store's `projects/` folder, only folders with CIVIC's own receipt), with a test on a temporary store. The adapter then calls it. Adopting it in the adapter and deleting the existing 79 folders need the owner's approval.

## 5. The two features

### Source-to-element (S7)

- **Tagging.** In CIVIC's dev and preview builds, a Vite transform in `packages/vite-connector` adds `data-civic-source="<repo-relative file>:<line>:<column>"` to host JSX elements (React 19 dropped `_debugSource`, so the fiber cannot be relied on). Only for sources the manifest lists; never in a production build. Gui (Apache 2.0) is read for ideas, not depended on.
- **Element → source.** The overlay and canvas selection read the nearest tagged ancestor and show the file and line under "Details". Annotations and work requests store it as an optional `source: { file, line, column, revision }`, so `get_request` hands the agent the file to open.
- **Source → elements.** `civic elements <file>[:<from>-<to>]` and an MCP tool return the scenarios and elements a file or line range renders, from a capture's tagged DOM. A diff maps its hunks to line ranges and highlights those elements on the canvas.
- First on CIVIC's own screens (needs S6), then the synthetic examples; Orca and Laundry stay local, owner-run checks.

### Backend coverage (S8)

# 0022: Effect owns lifetimes, XState decides lifecycles, the data core stays plain

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Decider:** Owner's direction that CIVIC be an Effect + XState + Electron project like Orca; the boundaries decided by Claude as controller; the owner may revise them
- **Builds on:** [0006](0006-deterministic-civic-for-agentic-teams.md) (no model calls), [0010](0010-project-dependency-boundary.md) (project boundary), [0021](0021-civic-preview-reviews-a-worktree-of-civic.md) (`civic preview`)
- **Plan:** [rebuild plan](../plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md)

## Context

CIVIC's graph, importers and records are pure, tested functions. Its weak spots are the parts with a lifetime: previews, servers, workers, the desktop window and the request lifecycle, whose rules are `if` checks spread over files and whose timers and processes are cleaned up by hand. Orca solved the same problems with Effect for resources and XState for decisions.

## Decision

1. **Effect owns anything with a lifetime**: processes, listeners, workers, watchers, timers, the MCP server, the app server and Electron main. Timers use Effect `Schedule` and `Clock`, never raw `setTimeout`/`setInterval` outside browser UI glue.
2. **XState decides, it does not execute.** Durable lifecycles (work requests) go through a pure kernel: a transition may only emit intents, and the caller persists the new state with the record's version as compare-and-set. In-process lifecycles (preview, app server, run, desktop window) are `@xstate/effect` actors whose timers run on Effect's `Clock`.
3. **Every machine has a graph test** whose event list covers every event the machine declares.
4. **The data core stays plain.** `graph/` and `importers/` import neither Effect nor XState; a check enforces it. Effect `Schema` may replace hand validation there only where it deletes code.
5. **`@civic/core`** (`packages/core`) holds the kernel, the graph-test helper and shared Effect services. This replaces the 18 Oct plan's choice to keep everything in `@civic/canvas`, because `review/` and `packages/canvas` both need the kernel.
6. Pins follow Orca's workspace: `effect` and `@effect/platform-node` `~4.0.5`, `xstate` `6.0.0-alpha.73`, `@xstate/effect` `1.0.0-alpha.12`, `electron` `^45.3.2`, `vite-plus` `^1.6.0`.

CIVIC still makes no model calls and launches no agents. Integrations are the MCP server, skills and plugins that harnesses use.

## Consequences

- Recurring review corrections become lint rules or tests with baselines that may only shrink.
- The request machine replaces status checks in `review/src/loop.ts`; status changes outside it are refused by an architecture test.
- One install for all of CIVIC comes before Effect is used outside `packages/`, so one copy of Effect is loaded.

**The plan**
- **What stays:** the graph, importers and records code stays as plain functions. It works and is tested, and a new check will keep the new libraries out of it.
- **What moves:** the parts that start, watch and stop things move onto Effect and XState. That covers previews, servers, the desktop window, the MCP server and the request lifecycle.
- **Order:**
  1. Checks that stop old review mistakes coming back.
  2. One install for all of CIVIC.
  3. A shared state-machine core, then the request lifecycle built on it.
  4. The MCP server rebuilt on Effect.
  5. CIVIC as a project in its own picker.
  6. The two features (finding the code behind a selected element, and showing which server paths no journey reaches).
  7. The preview, app server and desktop window.

  Each step merges on its own once its checks pass.
- **Store growth:** the 79 stale Orca preview folders (1.4 GB) come from your private Orca preview adapter. It makes a new folder for every worktree and a new build on every change, and never deletes either. The fix is a shared cleanup helper in tracked code, which the adapter would then call.
- **One install:** I tested this on a throwaway workspace. The existing `packages/` workspace can take in `graph/`, `review/` and the other folders, so no root `package.json` is needed and your untracked one in the main checkout is safe.

**Running now (Codex workers)**
- [S1 Vite+ tooling for CIVIC](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A7f6fc551-6126-412c-836c-ac8e19bc3b4f): the Vite+ linter and test runner, commit hooks that require typed titles like `fix:` or `feat:`, and test lists found automatically instead of typed out by hand.

## 5b. CIVIC and Orca, both ways (S11b)

Owner, 15 Nov. Orca treats CIVIC as an outside integration it hands work to, as it treats Gui. CIVIC side: generic tools any coordinator can use, so CIVIC holds no Orca internals and names no Orca type. Orca is the first coordinator. CIVIC still makes no model calls and starts no agents; starting its own preview of a worktree is CIVIC's own work, as `civic preview` already does.

### Shared shapes

```ts
// A coordinator's work item, opaque to CIVIC. `system` is whatever the coordinator calls itself.
type WorkRef = { system: string; id: string; url?: string }

type ScreenRef = { project: string; scenario: string; journey?: string; route?: string }
type Shot = { viewport: 1440 | 390 | number; theme: 'light' | 'dark' }

type ChangedScreens = {
  revision: string; base: string
  screens: Array<ScreenRef & { because: Array<{ file: string; lines?: [number, number] }> }>
  limits: string[]          // e.g. files no capture renders, so no screen could be named
}

type ReviewSession = {
  id: string; workRef: WorkRef; line: string; revision: string
  link: string              // what the owner opens; loopback /review of that worktree's preview
  screens: Array<ScreenRef & { shots: Shot[] }>
}

type Coverage = {
  project: string; revision: string; evidenceAt: string
  screens: { total: number; covered: number; uncovered: ScreenRef[] }
  journeys: Array<{ id: string; screens: string[]; lastReplay: 'passed' | 'diverged' | 'none'; divergedAt?: number }>
  backend: {
    operations: Array<{ id: string; file: string; export: string; kind: 'server-function' | 'route' | 'rpc'; reachedBy: string[] }>
    unreached: string[]     // operation ids no passing replay reaches
  }
}
```

Work requests gain `links: WorkRef[]`. An annotation made in a review session carries that session's `workRef`, so the request it becomes is linked from birth.

### MCP surface

| Kind | Name | Input | Returns | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tool | `changed_screens` | `cwd`, `base` | `ChangedScreens` (source-to-element reverse map over the diff, plus journeys through those screens) | nothing |
| tool | `open_review` | `cwd`, `workRef`, `screens?` (default: `changed_screens`), `shots?` (default 1440 and 390, light and dark) | `ReviewSession` | starts or attaches that worktree's preview; no record |
| tool | `close_review` | `id` | — | stops the preview it started, by recorded process only |
| tool | `link_request` | request `id@version`, `workRef` | the request | adds one link; nothing else |
| tool | `list_requests` (existing) | adds `workRef?` filter | as today | nothing |
| tool | `coverage` | `cwd` or `project` | `Coverage` | nothing |
| resource | `civic://requests?system=…&id=…` | subscribable | requests linked to that work item | — |
| resource | `civic://coverage/{project}` | subscribable | `Coverage` | — |

Resource changes go out as `notifications/resources/updated`, so a coordinator waits on a notice instead of polling. The D35 write path is unchanged: `open_review` and `link_request` write no review outcome, and no coordinator or agent can resolve a request, accept a check or annotate on the owner's behalf.

### The three flows

1. **Orca asks for a review.** Orca calls `open_review` for a work item's worktree. The owner opens the link, comments, and each comment becomes a request linked to that work item. Orca hears it through the `civic://requests` resource and puts it on the work item.
2. **A CIVIC request becomes Orca work.** For a project Orca manages, Orca lists open requests, creates a work item from `get_request`'s work order, and calls `link_request`. Its agent then claims and reports through the existing tools.
3. **Orca's agents read coverage.** Through Orca's MCP gateway, agents call `coverage` (screens, journeys and backend) for the worktree they are in.

### Proposal for the Orca controller

Not built here; Orca is read-only for this work. In Orca's integration settings, register CIVIC's MCP server (`civic-mcp` over stdio, or the plugin's launcher). Add a "Review in CIVIC" action on a work item that calls `open_review` with the item's copy and shows `link` to the owner. Subscribe to `civic://requests` per open item, and turn new requests into notices or inputs on that item through Orca's own attention rules. Offer "Make a work item" on unlinked CIVIC requests for managed projects (flow 2). Pass `coverage` and `changed_screens` through the gateway to agents. Orca calls CIVIC; CIVIC never calls Orca.

## 6. Slices

import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { test } from 'node:test'
import { typed, untyped } from './commit-type.ts'

test('a commit title needs a conventional type; Git titles pass', () => {
  for (const title of ['fix: Keep the reason plain', 'feat(web)!: Show usage', 'chore: Bump deps\n\nBody', "Merge branch 'x'", 'Revert "fix: a"', 'fixup! fix: a', '# comment\nfeat: after a comment']) assert.ok(typed(title), title)
  for (const title of ['Keep the reason plain', 'fix:no space', 'Fix: capitalised type', 'wip: unknown type', '']) assert.ok(!typed(title), title)
})

test('only commits after main are checked', () => {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'civic-commit-type-'))
  const git = (...args: string[]) => execFileSync('git', ['-C', root, '-c', 'user.name=Fixture', '-c', 'user.email=f@example.invalid', '-c', 'commit.gpgsign=false', '-c', 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null', ...args], { encoding: 'utf8' })
  try {
    git('init', '-q', '-b', 'main')
    git('commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'Old untyped history')
    git('switch', '-q', '-c', 'work')
    git('commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'fix: Typed')
    assert.deepEqual(untyped(root), [])
    git('commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'Untyped change')
    assert.deepEqual(untyped(root), ['Untyped change'])
  } finally {
    rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })
  }
})
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

const TYPES = ['feat', 'fix', 'refactor', 'perf', 'test', 'docs', 'style', 'build', 'ci', 'chore', 'revert']
const TYPED = new RegExp(`^(?:${TYPES.join('|')})(?:\\([a-z0-9-]+\\))?!?: \\S`, 'u')
// Git writes these titles itself.
const GENERATED = /^(?:Merge |Revert "|fixup! |squash! |amend! )/u
const titleOf = (message: string) => message.split('\n').find(line => line.trim() !== '' && !line.startsWith('#')) ?? ''
export const typed = (message: string) => GENERATED.test(titleOf(message)) || TYPED.test(titleOf(message))
export const untyped = (root: string, base = 'main') => execFileSync('git', ['-C', root, 'log', '--format=%s', `${base}..HEAD`], { encoding: 'utf8' }).split('\n').filter(title => title !== '' && !typed(title))
export const advice = (titles: readonly string[]) => `Start each commit title with a type, like "fix: Keep the reason plain" (${TYPES.join(', ')}):\n${titles.map(title => `  ${title}`).join('\n')}`

if (import.meta.main) {
  const [file] = process.argv.slice(2)
  const bad = file === undefined ? untyped(fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url))) : [readFileSync(file, 'utf8')].flatMap(message => typed(message) ? [] : [titleOf(message)])
  if (bad.length > 0) {
    console.error(advice(bad))
    process.exitCode = 1
  }
}
import { globSync } from 'node:fs'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'

for (const file of globSync(['*.mjs', '*.cjs'], { cwd: process.argv[2] })) {
  const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--check', file], { stdio: 'inherit', cwd: process.argv[2] })
  if (result.error) throw result.error
  if (result.status !== 0) process.exit(result.status ?? 1)
}

I cleared out the stale preview folders and added both of your inputs to the plan and to the hooks work. The Vite+ branch still isn't committed: its full tests are queued until the machine's load drops.

**Store cleanup**
- 75 of the 79 folders belonged to Orca worktrees that no longer exist, so I moved them to your Trash. The project store went from about 1.4 GB to 139 MB.
- The space only comes back once you empty the Trash. Until then you can undo by dragging them back.
- I kept the 4 folders that match Orca worktrees still on disk: the main Orca checkout and three dogfood lanes.
- The old 3012 process (pid 8839) wasn't running, and nothing had these folders open.
- I couldn't truly delete them: the command guard blocks `rm -rf`, and I didn't try to get around it.
- I'll change your private Orca adapter to call the cleanup helper once the worker building it (S9b) finishes. Its receipts don't record which worktree they came from, so I matched folder names against your current Orca worktrees instead.

**XState checks**
- Every machine's test will check that every transition points at a real state, and that the machine has no serialization warnings.
- Any event sequence that ever fails gets saved as a fixture and replayed as a regression test. Fixtures are picked up automatically, never listed by hand.
- I'll read XState's built-in agent guide once it's installed, and use its command-line tools and codemod rather than writing our own.

**Git hooks**
- I switched to Orca's layout: the chaining file is gone, since Entire already chains to existing hooks. A new `commit-msg.pre-entire` file runs the real title check.
- AGENTS.md now says to point `core.hooksPath` at an absolute path.
- I haven't switched the hooks on yet. That setting is shared by every checkout, including your live one, so I'll turn it on only after this reaches main. Until then the hooks are untested.

These changes sit on the Vite+ branch with S1 and will be committed together once its tests pass.

The cleanup helper (S9b) is fixed and committed, but it isn't merged yet. It waits for the full sign-off, which can't run while the machine's load is 23.

- **The fix:** the worker's version would have refused every real Orca build. Those builds hold symlinked `node_modules`, and it treated any link inside a build as a reason to stop. It also gave up after scanning 10,000 files.
- **What it does now:** links inside a build are removed as links and never followed. The scan limit is 500,000 entries, and past that it deletes nothing. Linked store, project, receipt or build folders are still refused.
- **Tests:** a new test checks that a link pointing into another project is removed while that project's published build survives. All 21 local-package tests pass.
- **Committed:** signed on `fix/preview-build-retention`.

**Your Orca adapter will have to wait.** It loads its helpers from your main checkout, and the cleanup helper won't be there until this work reaches main. I won't merge into main from here, because that would change your live working copy. Once you merge, the adapter only needs two small changes: write the worktree path into each receipt, and call the cleanup after it publishes a build.

The full sign-offs for this and S1 start automatically once load drops below 6 and no Orca sign-off is running. I'm also holding off on starting new workers, since they would only make the machine busier.

content.text:
The checks-as-rules work (S2) is reviewed, fixed and committed, but not merged yet. The sign-off for CIVIC-in-its-own-picker (S6) is running now.

**Why tests had stalled:** my wait-for-quiet-machine check looked for any process with `bin/signoff` in its command line. The waiting script itself contained that text, so it blocked forever. That also stopped the S2 worker from running its tests. I stopped the stuck script and rewrote the check to match only a sign-off that is actually running.

**S2 results:**
- All 150 rules that were switched off are now on, measured against a recorded baseline. Today's code has 10,269 violations across 2,104 rule-and-file pairs.
- The check fails if any count grows or a new one appears. Lowering counts needs a deliberate `--update`, which can never raise a count.
- New architecture checks cover all tracked source:

  | Check | Today |
  |---|---|
  | `useEffect` in the UI | 51 |
  | raw timers in server code | 17 |
  | Effect, XState or process imports in graph or importers | 11 |
  | server imports from browser code | 7 |
  | module mocking | 0 |
  | imports from outside the repo | 0 |

- **One fix I made:** the pre-commit hook still ran plain lint, which would have blocked committing almost any existing file. It now runs the baseline check, which takes about 1.3 seconds. A clean change passes, and a change that adds a `useEffect` is refused.
- The worker never got to run the 9 test cases with a good and a bad sample for each rule; I ran them and they all pass.

**Order from here:** finish the S6 sign-off and merge it, then re-run the S3 layout test twice, then sign off and merge S3, then rebase and sign off S2. After that comes the shared state-machine core (S4), which needs S3's single install.
